issue.title: Monitor reconciliation's locked settle path runs a full-history artifact-index query per candidate via get_monitor()
issue.description:
DISCOVERED BY: bead sase-n7.4 during epic sase-n7 ('Get monitor reconciliation off the ACE startup critical path'), recorded as a PROPOSED FOLLOW-UP and routed to a task by sase-n7.land on 2026-08-16 (workspace sase_17, master HEAD 0ec2018f1).

WHAT IS WRONG: reconcile_dead_supervisor() (src/sase/monitor/reconcile.py:69) takes the lane lock and then calls get_monitor(record.lane, record.monitor_id) to re-read the record under the lock, and _reconcile_dead_supervisor_locked() re-reads through the same callable. get_monitor() (src/sase/monitor/store.py:246) walks _monitor_records() -> _project_records(), which issues an unbounded artifact-index query with include_full_history=True, active_limit=None, recent_completed_limit=None, include_hidden=True over ~/.sase/agent_artifact_index.sqlite, then linear-scans the result for the one artifact_dir it already knows. That is O(archive) work per settled candidate. On the author's real state that query measured 1.51 s per call against a 115 MB index (see the epic plan plan:202608/tui_startup_monitor_reconcile.md, Defect 3), and the index only grows.

WHY IT SURVIVED sase-n7: the epic bounded the query that *selects* reconciliation candidates (_reconciliation_monitor_records(), sase commit 9fe82045d) and moved the whole pass off the synchronous TUI disk load (39bdd6772), so this call is no longer on the ACE startup critical path. It is still archive-scaled work inside the settle path, and it multiplies by the number of dead-supervisor candidates -- exactly the burst case after a reboot, when many monitors need settling at once. The reconcile pass also holds the lane lock across it.

THE FIX ALREADY HAS A HOME: read_monitor_marker(project_name, artifacts_dir) (src/sase/monitor/store.py:257) exists for precisely this shape and documents it -- 'get_monitor() runs a full-history, unlimited, hidden-inclusive index query ... to find one record it already knows the path to'. The reconcile path holds the member's artifacts_dir, so the locked settle and re-read should use the marker helper instead of get_monitor(). Note reconcile_dead_supervisor() takes get_monitor as an injected GetMonitor callable, so the change is at the call sites in src/sase/monitor/store.py (reconcile_dead_supervisors, active_monitor_for_lane, monitor_blocking_start_for_lane) plus any test doubles, not a signature change. Confirm the marker read preserves the semantics the locked re-read depends on (it must still observe a concurrent settle and bail when the record already left 'running'); if it cannot, say so and keep get_monitor() with a bounded query instead.

SCOPE: switch the locked settle/re-read to the path-direct marker helper (or an equivalently bounded lookup), keep settlement semantics unchanged -- a monitor whose supervisor died must still settle, pre-reboot monitors must still reconcile to 'lost' -- and pin the new bound with a test asserting the reconcile pass does not scale its artifact-index queries with candidate count, mirroring tests/monitor/test_monitor_store_reconcile.py::test_reconcile_dead_supervisors_uses_bounded_active_monitor_index_query and ::test_reconcile_dead_supervisors_reads_proc_store_once.

IMPACT: background monitor settlement stays archive-dependent and gets slower as the artifact index grows, and a post-reboot burst pays that cost once per candidate while holding the lane lock. Not user-visible as a startup stall today, which is why it is a task rather than epic work.

payload.entry: RELATED: sase-n7 — the epic that surfaced this. Its phases bounded the reconciliation candidate query (9fe82045d) and moved the pass off the synchronous ACE disk load (39bdd6772), which is why this residual O(archive) call is no longer a startup stall and was routed to a task instead of being finished as epic work.

RELATED: sase-m9 — carries a DISCOVERED ISSUE note for the sibling defect in the same file: active_monitor_for_lane and monitor_blocking_start_for_lane (src/sase/monitor/store.py:143,165) do one full proc-store read per candidate. Both defects live on the same CLI lane-inspection call paths and reach get_monitor() through the same reconcile_dead_supervisor() call, so whoever fixes either should read the other first to avoid a collision.

RELATED: sase-kh — 'Prune or archive hidden agent-artifact index rows: 4,706 of 6,775 rows are hidden and nothing ever removes them'. That bead attacks the same growth curve from the data side; this bead attacks it from the query side. Fixing sase-kh would shrink the cost of the query but not remove the per-candidate O(archive) scan.

Fixed by epic sase-ns.6.6 phase sase-ns.6.6.3 (commit 2f41353b5). Verified in source: every reconcile call site in src/sase/monitor/store.py now injects the path-direct read_monitor_marker() instead of get_monitor() -- reconcile_dead_supervisors (line 416), active_monitor_for_lane (234), monitor_blocking_start_for_lane (267), and stop_monitor's three dead-supervisor branches (305, 313, 321). read_monitor_marker's signature (project_name, artifacts_dir) -> MonitorRecord | None matches the GetMonitor alias in reconcile.py:46, so the locked settle in reconcile_dead_supervisor (line 78) and the locked re-read in _reconcile_dead_supervisor_locked (line 123) both stay path-direct; no signature changed. get_monitor() itself is unchanged and still exported. The archive-scaled per-candidate index query the bead measured at 1.51s is gone from the settle path. Bound pinned by test_reconcile_dead_supervisors_settle_path_index_queries_do_not_scale_with_candidates (3 vs 8 candidates, exactly one artifact-index query) in tests/monitor/test_monitor_store_reconcile_queries.py, which is the file dc221a458 had just split out. Settlement semantics confirmed unchanged: dead supervisor still settles to failed, pre-reboot still reconciles to lost, and a concurrent on-disk settle is observed rather than overwritten.
